title: Check RMS disconnected AGV count and identify likely disconnect cause (lost RMS comms vs turned off)
summary: On the RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary, read the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric. Use the training’s definition to interpret “disconnected” as AGVs that have lost communication from RMS (RMS runs on the server; AGVs are on Wi‑Fi), then correlate the disconnected count with likely causes: Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss vs AGVs being turned off.
when_to_use: When you need a first-pass diagnostic using RMS’s disconnected AGV count to understand whether AGVs are likely disconnected due to lost RMS/Wi‑Fi communication versus being turned off.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as the only evidence to confirm a specific root cause when the disconnected count is high and you cannot determine whether it is communication loss or AGVs being turned off (requires additional evidence beyond this metric).
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the RMS / fleet status UI checks and interpret the disconnected AGV count using the provided definition.
L2_support: Assist when the disconnected count is high and the cause cannot be determined from this metric alone.

system_preconditions: RMS / fleet status UI is reachable and displaying the map monitor summary area that includes the disconnected AGV count.

visual_references.description: Map Monitor Message Panel area showing the metric list including “Count of AGVs disconnected”.

steps.title: Open RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary area
steps.purpose: Get to the UI location where the disconnected AGV count metric is shown.
steps.instruction: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui) and navigate to the map monitor summary/message panel area that includes the “count of AGVs disconnected” metric.
steps.expected_result: The RMS UI shows the map monitor summary/message panel with a visible “count of AGVs disconnected” value.
steps.healthy_condition: The map monitor summary/message panel is visible and the disconnected AGV count metric is readable.
steps.failure_condition: The disconnected AGV count metric is not visible/readable (e.g., wrong screen/section, hidden panel).

actions.label: Open RMS map monitor summary
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (map monitor summary area).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “The next one is the count of Agvs that are disconnected… The next one is the count of Agvs that are disconnected, right?”
Map Monitor Message Panel includes “Count of AGVs disconnected”.

steps.title: Read the “count of AGVs disconnected” value
steps.purpose: Quantify how many AGVs RMS believes are disconnected.
steps.instruction: In the RMS map monitor summary/message panel, locate and read the “count of AGVs disconnected” value.
steps.expected_result: You have the numeric value for “count of AGVs disconnected” as shown in the RMS UI.
steps.healthy_condition: A single disconnected count value is displayed in the metric list.
steps.failure_condition: The disconnected count value is missing, inconsistent with the UI state, or cannot be read.

actions.label: Locate disconnected count
actions.exact_action: Locate and read the “disconnected” AGV count.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “The next one is the count of Agvs that are disconnected, right?”
Map Monitor Message Panel shows “Count of AGVs disconnected”.

steps.title: Interpret “disconnected” as lost RMS communication (RMS server + AGVs on Wi‑Fi)
steps.purpose: Ensure the disconnected count is interpreted correctly before correlating causes.
steps.instruction: Use the definition: treat “disconnected” as AGVs that have lost communication from RMS (RMS is the application running on the server; AGVs are on the Wi‑Fi).
steps.expected_result: Your interpretation of the disconnected count is explicitly tied to lost communication from RMS to AGVs over Wi‑Fi.
steps.healthy_condition: You can state that “disconnected” means lost communication from RMS to AGVs (RMS server application; AGVs on Wi‑Fi).
steps.failure_condition: You interpret “disconnected” as something unrelated to RMS communication loss (e.g., not tied to RMS/Wi‑Fi).

actions.label: Apply disconnected definition
actions.exact_action: Use the training definition: treat “disconnected” as AGVs that have lost communication from RMS (RMS is the application running on the server; AGVs are on the Wi‑Fi).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “So what does it mean disconnected? It means that Agvs have lost communication from RMS… RMS is the… application running on the server. The Agvs are on the Wi‑Fi.”
“Agvs have lost communication from RMS… RMS… application running on the server… The Agvs are on the Wi‑Fi.”

“Disconnected AGV count indicates how many AGVs RMS considers disconnected. RMS is the server application, AGVs communicate over Wi‑Fi, and disconnects can result from communication loss or an AGV being turned off.”

steps.title: Correlate disconnected count with likely causes: Wi‑Fi/RMS comms loss vs AGV turned off
steps.purpose: Generate likely cause hypotheses that match the disconnected count definition.
steps.instruction: Correlate the disconnected count with likely causes: (1) AGVs lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on site, or (2) the AGV was turned off.
steps.expected_result: You produce a likely cause hypothesis that matches one of the two causes explicitly described: Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss or AGV turned off.
steps.healthy_condition: Your hypothesis aligns with the observed situation (e.g., if AGVs were turned off, you expect to see disconnect; if not, you consider Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot correlate the disconnected count to either communication loss with site Wi‑Fi or AGVs being turned off.

actions.label: Correlate likely cause
actions.exact_action: Correlate the disconnected count with likely causes mentioned in the training: (1) AGV lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on the site itself, or (2) it was turned off.

stop_or_escalate_if: Disconnected count is high and you cannot determine whether the cause is communication loss vs AGVs being turned off (requires additional evidence beyond this metric).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “The disconnection can be like has the AGB lost communication with the Wi‑Fi on the site itself, right. Or it was turned… it was turned off.”
“if we look at this side right now, if we turn off AGV, we know that we have turned it off. So I expect to see disconnect.”
“disconnects can result from communication loss or an AGV being turned off.”

success_criteria: You can read the RMS “count of AGVs disconnected” metric from the RMS / fleet status UI.
You interpret “disconnected” as lost communication from RMS to AGVs over Wi‑Fi.
You correlate the disconnected count to one of the two explicitly described likely causes: Wi‑Fi/RMS communication loss or AGV turned off.
healthy_conditions: RMS map monitor summary shows a readable “count of AGVs disconnected” value.
Your cause hypothesis matches the situation: if AGVs were turned off, disconnected count is expected; otherwise, communication loss with site Wi‑Fi is the likely cause.
failure_conditions: Disconnected count is high and you cannot determine whether the cause is communication loss vs AGVs being turned off using only this metric.
escalation_guidance: If the disconnected count is high and you cannot determine whether the cause is communication loss vs AGVs being turned off, stop and escalate for additional evidence beyond this metric (involve L2_support).

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: Map Monitor Message Panel metric list; locate the “Count of AGVs disconnected” item and its value.
